summary: H-Anim is an international standard in two parts for describing humanoid characters. The first part defines the abstract structure of a figure: a root object, named joints and segments in a hierarchy, attachment sites and morph-target displacers, with levels of articulation that set how much joint detail a figure has. The second part defines how recorded motion-capture data or keyframes are attached to such a figure and exchanged between characters. It leaves the file form, mesh shapes, appearance and rendering to the system that embeds the figure through a binding, and it says nothing about identity, sound or the real world. It defines no network protocol, though the motion-data part notes that animation data can be exchanged through networks. A trap for a standards audience: the standard describes structure and motion, not a finished avatar file, so a figure is portable only where the receiving system implements a binding, and animation data is promised to be shareable only between figures that have the same skeletal configuration.

coverage.note: It carries the articulated structure, the skin binding fields and a description with author and usage terms, but it does not define the mesh shapes or the appearance itself, which are left to the representation system.
